text:
alice: Heads up — prod saw a CPU tail on hosts serving model-x yesterday during streaming requests. +15% host CPU for the ingress parser/tokenizer path. Anyone else see this?
ben: saw the alert. spikes correlate with long-stream chat sessions (chunked responses).
carmen: timeline? was this after the kernel selection tweak yesterday?
alice: yes, rolled kernel picker change at ~10:12 UTC. spike started ~10:20 and persisted on ~30% of hosts.
dave: profile dump from one affected host:

perf-bot: flamegraph snippet:
```
parse_frame             35.2%
kv_cache_lookup         12.1%
tokenize_stream         18.4%
grpc_read               8.9%
writev_coalesce         6.0%
others                  19.4%
```

ben: interesting that tokenize_stream is high — our earlier hypothesis was kernel mismatch causing sticky minibatches, but this points to host-side overhead.
carmen: could be batching heuristics interacting badly with continuous streaming; maybe batcher holds longer trying to coalesce fragments then parse cost grows.
ben: from traces, kernel selector chose FP16-quant path for these requests (model length ~1024). new heuristic bumps preference for that path because of latency median improvements. Wonder if the lightweight tokenizer code path is slower under that kernel due to different seq-length assumptions.
dave: also seeing increased syscalls: lots of small reads -> http2 framing + grpc hpack decode. file descriptor read patterns show many sub-1k reads.
alice: I ran a quick pprof on the parse thread — stack shows repeated utf8-normalize + slice-copy during chunk assembly. here's small repro command I used:
```
stress-client --model model-x --stream --msgs 50 --avg-chunk 128 --concurrency 8 --duration 5m
```

carmen: can we try toggling kernel picker to prefer the fat-kernel (old path) on a canary host and compare CPU?
ben: will do. also want to collect KV cache hit rates — if cache miss spike, tokenizer may reparse prefixes causing work.
dave: grabbing KV metrics now. initial glance: per-host kvcache hit rate dropped from 98% -> 88% for affected hosts in the window. not huge but explanatory.

alice: so likely combination: kernel change -> slightly different batching behavior -> more fragments -> lower KV reuse -> more parse/token work + more small grpc reads -> overhead.
ben: plan: 1) roll back kernel picker on one hostgroup 2) enable writev coalescing patch (unreleased) on another 3) increase kvcache grace window to 250ms for a canary set to see hit rate impact.
carmen: add histogram of sequence length distribution to telemetry so we can see if kernel heuristic mismatch thresholds need retuning.
dave: applying kvcache grace window change to canary now. will post metrics in 5m.
alice: small suggestion: add lightweight fast-path in tokenizer for already-normalized ASCII to avoid utf8-normalize on common chat payloads — cheap win.
ben: noted. I'll file small PR: tokenizer:avoid-normalize-if-ascii.
dave: canary results: after kvcache grace window bump, host CPU dropped ~6% and kvcache hit back to ~96% on canary. good signal.
carmen: ok looks like heuristic interplay. we should add an experiment matrix to prevent kernel picker rollouts without kvcache + batching experiments.
alice: agree. followups: ben to open rollback PR if canary fat-kernel reduces CPU further; ben to instrument batching latency windows; carmen to add seq-len telemetry; dave to keep kvcache telemetry for 24h.
ben: I'll also add a tracer tag when kernel selector picks a non-default path so it's easy to filter traces.
alice: thanks team — keeping an eye on rollout. :thumbsup:
